summary: SafeVault Phase 2 Sprint 2 (SQLite + MetadataManager + one-time migration) verified end-to-end. Static inspection of all 5 new/modified files matches spec (metro alias, web stub, sqlite driver with dynamic native import + web webStub, MetadataManager with SHA-256 that omits updatedAt + backup rotation + ManifestCorruptedError, migration with idempotent flag, VaultContext try/catch-wrapped Migration.runIfNeeded call and unchanged public API). tsc --noEmit exit 0. Metro web entry bundle returns HTTP 200 (~12MB). Frontend.err.log shows only pre-existing shadow*/expo-notifications/RNGoogleSignIn warnings. Runtime E2E on 420x900: splash → login-demo → onboarding-continue → home with priority-reminder-card + all regression tabs (home/timeline/docs/profile/tab-add-fab). localStorage['safevault.migration.v2.completed']='true' after boot1 (via unsupported-platform branch as designed on web). On reload, no '[migration] v2 completed:' log appears and flag remains 'true' — idempotency confirmed. 7/7 in-process manifest unit tests pass (buildEmptyManifest defaults, validateManifest(null) errors, validateManifest(empty)=[], 64-char lowercase-hex SHA-256, hash stable across updatedAt mutation, hash changes when documents change).
critical_code_review_comments: Minor: on web, Migration.runIfNeeded() returns ranMigration=false with skippedReason='unsupported-platform', so the '[migration] v2 completed:' console line never fires on web boots. This is consistent with the spec (log only when res.ranMigration is true) — but web-only observability of the flag-set relies on inspecting localStorage. Consider a debug log for the 'unsupported-platform' branch behind __DEV__.

Nice-to-have: metadataManager.save() rotates backup even when rotation download fails — the catch just warns and continues; if primary write later fails, backup could hold arbitrarily stale data. Acceptable for Sprint 2 (best-effort noted in comment).
seed_data_creation: None — used existing demo seed and vault data.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Sprint 2 groundwork verified. On web, SQLite is a no-op (webStub) so migration marks the flag via unsupported-platform branch — this is by design. Sprint 3 will begin reading/writing through SQLite/manifest; VaultContext public API is currently unchanged (reads/writes still via AsyncStorage). To re-run migration on native, call Migration._resetMigrationFlagForTests. Manifest hash primitives are in /app/frontend/__tests__/manifest.test.mjs.
